newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHORT-TERM RATES DOWN AHEAD OF BOND AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHORT-TERM RATES DOWN AHEAD OF BOND AUCTION.

text.p: Greek short-term depos and forex forwards were heading lower in early dealings ahead of today's auction of three-, five-, seven-year paper and the first ever 10-year fixed coupon bond, dealers said.
Ecu/drachma was trading in the narrow 309.0/15 range in quiet dealings. Monday was a market holiday in Greece.
"Short-term interbank rates are down," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Tomnext has fallen about half a point on Friday's forex inflows, possibly linked to OTE telecom's IPO."
About 100 million ecus and 100 million marks were sold for drachmas at the fixing on Friday.

"Short-term rates are driven by liquidity which has been boosted lately and the market expects the central bank to leave more funds into the system on Wednesday, if necessary, given an outflow of 310 billion drachmas due to the auction," a dealer said.
Bond dealers said the auction would be a success and they expected bids for three-, five-and seven-year paper to follow closely secondary bond prices with an upward bias.
Dealers said bids for the three-year bond, the most popular instrument among fixed coupon bonds locally, would range from 99 to 100.7.

"The market needs a benchmark and wants to see the auction of the 10-year bond succeed," said a bond dealer. "The fact that the amount is small, just 100 billion drachmas, will help the ministry get better bids."
Dealers said they expected bids around par for the 10-year coupon bond.
"It is known that some state pension funds will place bids for the 10-year bond at par," said a bond trader. "This combined with the small amount makes me believe that bids will hover around par."
Greece will auction 100 billion drachmas of 10-year, 8.80 percent fixed coupon bonds. It is Greece's first ever issue of 10-year drachma-denominated bonds.
It also re-opens bids for three-year, 9.8 percent bonds, five-year, 9.2 percent bonds and seven-year, 8.9 percent bonds. Fifty billion drachmas for each maturity are auctioned.
The mark was quoted at 158.00/10 from Friday's 158.440 fix, the dollar at 274.09/19 drachmas from 274.120 and the ecu at 309.15/25 from 309.160 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma opened at 309.0/05 and trades currently around 309.05/10 in quiet dealings," said a forex trader at a foreign bank.
The National Bank of Greece quoted the following early rates:
** Overnight at 11.20-11.70
** One week at 11.10-11.60
** Two weeks at 11.15-11.65
** Three weeks at 11.20-11.70
** One month at 11.20-11.70
** Two months at 11.00-11.50
** Three months at 10.80-11.30
** Six months at 10.50-11.00
** Nine months at 10.30-10.80
** Twelve months at 10.20-10.70
--Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
